chunks: "I think about rework in five buckets.
First, replacing a component : that could be a through-hole part with an iron and a desoldering pump, an SMD part with hot air, or a BGA or QFN with a rework station and X-ray afterwards.
Second, changing connections : cutting a trace with a knife and adding a bodge wire to make a connection the layout missed.
Third, changing population : swapping a resistor value, fitting a footprint that wasn't populated, or removing a part.
Fourth, repairs : fixing a lifted pad or a damaged trace with a wire or a pad kit.
And fifth, cleanup : removing a solder bridge, cleaning flux, or removing conformal coating to get to a part. Each one has a risk. Part swaps stress pads.
Wires add inductance, so I would happily bodge a slow GPIO or enable line but I would avoid a wire on a DDR clock or a switching node.
And if I know a connection might need to change, I'd rather design in a zero-ohm link or an extra footprint than depend on cutting a trace.
When I do a modification, I'd also document it so the next board spin includes the fix."
